title: Mass Spectrometry-based Immune Profiling in Autoimmune Diseases
off: Mass Spectrometry-based Immune Profiling in Peripheral Blood of Autoimmune Diseases
collabs: National Natural Science Foundation of China
Zhejiang PuLuoTing Health Technology Co., Ltd.
summary: Based on mass spectrometry flow method, this study analyzed the typing of new T, B, NK and DC cell subsets in peripheral blood of common autoimmune diseases and their correlation with disease activity, aiming at establishing an early screening and diagnosis model of autoimmune diseases.
desc: The study will include patients with systemic lupus erythematosus, Sjogren's syndrome, inflammatory myopathy, systemic sclerosis, vasculitis, rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, osteoarthritis and gouty arthritis and healthy controls. About 50 patients of each type are required. The patients are in a state of disease activity and do not use biological agents. Their peripheral blood will be detected by mass spectrometry.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Male or female, and aged 18-70 at the time of screening interview (inclusive).
2. The diagnosis of each disease meets the following standards - Systemic lupus erythematosus: 1997 ACR lupus classification standard

   * Behcet's disease: 2014 ICBD Behcet's disease classification standard
   * ANCA-associated vasculitis: 1990 American College of Rheumatology Classification Standard
   * Rheumatoid arthritis: 1987 ARA classification standard
   * Ankylosing spondylitis: new york standard revised in 1984
   * Sjogren's syndrome: 2016 ACR/EULAR Sjogren's syndrome classification standard
   * Inflammatory myopathy: Bohan recommended criteria in 1977
   * Systemic sclerosis: SSc standard formulated by American Rheumatology Association in 1980.
   * Psoriatic arthritis: CASPAR standard in 2006
   * Gouty arthritis: 1997 ACR gout classification standard
3. Disease activity status, each disease should meet the disease activity index;
4. Glucocorticoid (≤1mg/kg/d prednisone or other hormones with equivalent dose) was used before joining the group, and DMARDs (such as methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, leflunomide, cyclosporine, etc.) were allowed;
5. When participating in the trial, the patient must be informed in writing and hope that the patient can abide by the requirements of the research follow-up plan and other protocols.

   Exclusion Criteria:

1\. Use IVIg or cyclophosphamide within 1.2 months, use other biological agents (infliximab, adalimumab, etanercept, anakinra, etc.) within 3 months, and use rituximab within 6 months; 2.1 months after receiving high-dose glucocorticoid (\> 1 mg/kg/d). 3. Serious complications: including heart failure (≥ NYHA III), renal insufficiency (creatinine clearance rate ≤30 ml/min) and hepatic insufficiency (serum ALT or AST is greater than three times the normal upper limit, or total bilirubin is greater than the normal upper limit).

4\. Other serious, progressive or uncontrollable hematological, gastrointestinal, endocrine, lung, heart, nerve or brain diseases (including demyelinating diseases, such as multiple sclerosis).

5\. Suffering from serious infection (including but not limited to hepatitis, pneumonia, bacteremia, pyelonephritis, EB virus, tuberculosis infection), or being hospitalized due to infection, or using intravenous antibiotics to treat infection 2 months before the first dose of treatment.

6\. Chest imaging showed abnormalities of malignant tumor or current active infection (including tuberculosis) within 3 months before enrollment.

7\. Infected with HIV(HIV antibody positive serology) or hepatitis C (Hep C antibody positive serology). If the serum is positive, it is recommended to consult a doctor with expertise in treating HIV or hepatitis C virus infection.

8\. Any known malignant tumor or history of malignant tumor in the past 5 years. 9. Received any vaccination within 3 months before joining the group.

x.titre: Immunophénotypage par cytométrie de masse dans les maladies auto-immunes
x.question: Les sous-populations de cellules immunitaires du sang, mesurées par cytométrie de masse, permettent-elles de distinguer les maladies auto-immunes et d'en suivre l'activité ?
x.contexte:
Les maladies auto-immunes systémiques et rhumatismales (lupus, Sjögren, myosites, sclérodermie, vascularites, polyarthrite rhumatoïde, spondylarthrite, rhumatisme psoriasique, goutte) partagent des symptômes et un diagnostic parfois tardif. Les biomarqueurs actuels sont souvent peu spécifiques.

La cytométrie de masse permet de caractériser en une seule analyse des dizaines de marqueurs sur les lymphocytes T, B, NK et les cellules dendritiques, avec une résolution bien supérieure à la cytométrie classique.

Cette étude observationnelle de l'hôpital People's de l'université de Pékin prévoit d'inclure environ 500 adultes, environ 50 par maladie, en poussée et sans biothérapie, ainsi que des témoins sains. Elle cherche à décrire de nouveaux sous-types cellulaires, leur lien avec l'activité de la maladie et à construire un modèle de dépistage et de diagnostic précoces.
x.interet: Si des signatures immunitaires reproductibles sont identifiées, elles pourraient aider au diagnostic précoce et au suivi de l'activité. Il s'agit d'une recherche exploratoire monocentrique.
x.profil: Des adultes de 18 à 70 ans atteints de maladies rhumatismales auto-immunes actives, et des témoins sains.
inclusion: Diagnostic selon les critères de classification propres à chaque maladie
Maladie active selon l'indice d'activité de chaque maladie
Corticoïdes ≤ 1 mg/kg/j d'équivalent prednisone ; DMARDs conventionnels autorisés
Consentement écrit et respect du suivi
exclusion: Immunoglobulines IV ou cyclophosphamide < 1,2 mois, autres biothérapies < 3 mois, rituximab < 6 mois
Corticothérapie à forte dose (> 1 mg/kg/j) récente
Insuffisance cardiaque NYHA ≥ III, clairance < 30 mL/min, atteinte hépatique
Autre maladie grave ou non contrôlée (dont maladie démyélinisante)
Infection grave récente (dont tuberculose, EBV) ou hospitalisation pour infection
Cancer ou infection active sur l'imagerie thoracique
